# Twitter / X — 2009

**The last full year before the life the rest of this wiki is about.** 2009
opens on a twenty-year-old finishing an audio degree in Winter Park and closes
on a twenty-one-year-old in love, driving I-95 north with a girlfriend the
corpus will still be documenting sixteen years later. Between those two points
the account records the end of school, the first sustained studio practice, a
dated departure from the Republican party, and — in its last six weeks — the
beginning of the relationship that becomes the control case for every
attachment question the wiki asks. What it does **not** record is the thing
that arrives seven weeks after the final tweet: Suboxone, 17 February 2010.
2009 is the year immediately upstream of that, written from inside it by
somebody who did not know it was coming.

**Read the Gaps section before believing any pattern on this page.** The first
nine months are not a sample of 2009. They are a sample of the last two days
of each month, and the distinction is the difference between a finding and an
artifact.

## School ends, and the record says it ends later than the wiki does

The Full Sail material runs the whole year and it is unglamorous: *"surround
sound lecture"* (26 January), *"48 hours of hell is about to begin"* into
*"1 down bitttches. Studying all night"* (26–27 February), the Songcraft
final, an ESA lecture, and the flat indignity of *"learning how to wrap
cables. are you kidding me fs?"* (31 March) — a paying student annoyed at
being taught the trade's most menial physical skill.

Two dates on this page contradict the graduation date the rest of the wiki
carries. On **31 August 2009** he writes *"so weirded out i start my last
month of college tomorrow. having multiple reality checks."* — which places
the final month in **September**, not August. And in December he is plainly
still enrolled: *"pro tools lab. noice"* (30 November), *"aced my practical
without headphones"* (14 December), *"in class...."* (15 December), *"long
day of class tomorrow"* (17 December), and on **19 December** *"taking aws
final with it."*

> **CONTRADICTION [2026-09-03]:** `raw/self/context-core/CONTEXT_CORE_EXPANDED.md`
> states *"AS Recording Arts; graduated Aug 2009 (top 5%)"*, and
> `wiki/timeline/periods/full-sail-2008-2010` and `wiki/people/alexis-armel`
> both build on that date. The contemporaneous public record contradicts it in
> two independent places: a "last month of college" beginning 1 September, and
> coursework with a final examination running to 19 December. The two cannot
> both be true. The record here is dated, first-person and contemporaneous;
> the August date is first-person testimony given years later. **Neither is
> corrected on the strength of the other** — the disagreement is held, and the
> only artefact that would settle it is a Full Sail transcript, which the
> corpus does not have. The narrow claim this page will support is that Dan
> was still taking classes and sitting finals in December 2009.

Note what is *not* in dispute: the top-5% class standing, which nothing here
touches either way.

## The studio year

This is the year music production stops being a subject and becomes a
practice. It opens with the comparison already made in the language of the
industry he wants into — *"my life is literally like FBR now- no food, no
sleep, just records"* (12 January, Fueled By Ramen) — and proceeds through an
Afterplayrewind recording session (31 March), *"planning all the money i'm
gonna spend on this minimicro home studio"* (30 April), *"Day 1 of rtn shit.
Scratch tracks and drums today"* (30 June), and *"8am i'm still awake working
on a song"* (30 October). On **31 October**, the night before his
twenty-first birthday, he states the ambition outright and hedges it in the
same breath: *"maybe I'll one day be a hip hop producer. maybe I'll one day be
pow enough for @djgenie."*

He also talks *to* the musicians he listens to rather than only about them —
`@markhoppus` of Blink-182 gets a joke about studio interns (31 March),
`@GabrielSaporta` of Cobra Starship gets an album endorsement (31 July). The
distance between fan and participant is already something he does not
observe.

## Politics: a dated exit, eleven years before the arrival

On **28 November 2009**, linking out twice in succession, he writes:

> *"people like this are why i no longer consider myself a republican...wowwwwwwwww"*

This is the earliest dated political self-description in the corpus, and its
shape matters more than its date. It is a **departure, not an arrival** — he
says what he has stopped being, names no replacement, and the sentence is
triggered by *people*, by a link to somebody behaving badly, rather than by an
argument or a policy. `wiki/mind/synthesis/2020-left-turn` dates the arrival
of the democratic-socialist identity to 22 August 2020 and has since found a
second causal account in 2022 — the O&A fanbase splitting rightward and
repelling him leftward, also a departure from a tribe. The 2009 line is the
same mechanism, running eleven years earlier against the tribe he was raised
in: `CONTEXT_CORE_EXPANDED` records a *"Republican household + talk-radio diet
(Limbaugh/Beck/Hannity)"*. **The exit is old; only the destination is new.**

The caution is that one tweet is one tweet. It is not evidence of a 2009
left turn, nothing else on this page is political, and the eleven-year gap
between leaving and arriving is itself the finding rather than a problem with
it.

## Balloon Boy, and watching the coverage instead of the event

On **15 October 2009** a six-year-old was believed to be aboard a runaway
helium balloon over Colorado. Dan posted through the whole day, and almost
nothing he wrote is about the child:

> *"reasons why i love this country: #1- little kids in hot air balloons
> bombing around denver. #2- popcorn"*
> *"HIS NAME IS FALCON. OMG perfect"*
> *"watching CNN on delay via a paused DVR. this is a little bit riveting."*
> *"smoke one for balloon boy. the best one-off meme ever."*

The subject is the coverage, the naming, the DVR, and the object's status as a
**meme** — a word he applies to a live news event on the day it happens.
`wiki/mind/synthesis/millennial-digital-witness` dates the underlying
disposition to a Hurricane Sandy tweet of 30 October 2012 and calls it
*"fourteen years older than the theory"*. This is the same disposition three
years earlier still.

It is a **weaker instance than Sandy and must not be filed as an equal one.**
The 2012 line names the category — *"first true 'digital disaster'"*, *"so
much user generated content"* — and is a claim about the medium. The 2009 day
demonstrates the habit without ever stating it: he watches the watching, and
does not say that he is doing so. The precise correction to the synthesis is
that the *habit* is at least seventeen years old rather than fourteen, while
the *articulation* stays where that page put it.

## The last six weeks: "her", then a name

The year's final act is a relationship starting in real time, and it is
already fully mined on `wiki/people/alexis-armel` — the unnamed *"her"* of
29–30 November in Pennsylvania, the first `@alexisarmel` tweet on 14 December
(*"you amaze me. can't believe you're real"*, and separately *"dan in
love."*), *"i have the most amaaaazing girlfriend"* two days later, Seven
Springs on 22 December, and *"d&a's first christmas"* on the 25th. Eleven days
from the first use of her name to a shared Christmas presented as an
established unit.

What this page adds is the **surrounding weather**, which the relationship
tables cannot carry: he is sick for most of December, driving between two
states, sitting finals, and writing *"i'm so blessed"* on Christmas Day. The
speed is not the speed of a man with nothing else going on. It is the speed of
a man doing everything at once and putting the relationship at the front of
it.

## Pennsylvania, and the shuttle

The account moves physically all year and hates one end of the trip. October:
*"packing/getting house in order"*, the airport bit about *"businessmen
things: expense reduction! bottom line! coffee!"*, then home for Saw VI, a
Steelers game and Halloween. November: back for Thanksgiving, Pitt–WVU with
`@joshbrannan` (*"my true love"*), *"pennsylvania, what's a stoner to do?!"*.
December: the drive north on the 19th *"in the most hyped storm evar"*, then
the I-95 run back south on the 30th, narrated in numbered *"road update"*
posts. He is at home in Pennsylvania and unwilling to be there, which is the
same posture 2008 recorded in cruder words (*"i fucking hate going home"*).

The Western Pennsylvania identity is intact underneath the complaint —
Steelers throughout, *"PENS"*, *"yeaaaaah malkin"*, Big Ben called *"a mark
ass bitch"* mid-game, the Backyard Brawl. Leaving the place did not touch the
allegiances.

## Two lines on the same day, at twenty

On **22 October 2009**, nine days before turning twenty-one, he posts *"retire
by 25"* and, hours later, *"country club status. bloated sense of self
worth."* Both are jokes. Neither is only a joke: the first is a timeline with
a deadline on it and the second is a diagnosis of the person holding the
timeline, and the corpus's later account of how Dan measures himself — an
on/off verdict with no middle setting, a countdown running underneath it — is
recognisable in both at twenty years old, sixteen years before anybody wrote
it down as a finding.

## Cannabis is everywhere here, and opiates are nowhere

Cannabis is continuous and casual across the year: *"Jester thinks I have
swine flu and won't share a spliff"* (30 April), *"smoke one for balloon boy"*
(15 October), *"pennsylvania, what's a stoner to do?!"* (25 November),
*"sour diesel"* among the things he is thankful for (26 November), *"can't
wait to get home and smoke this kush"* (30 November), *"i'm high as a
motherfucker, flyyy as a motherfucker"* (28 December).

**There is not one opiate reference on this page.** That is a negative result
worth stating plainly rather than an absence worth passing over, because
`CONTEXT_CORE_EXPANDED` dates the first opiate — Roxicet, then Oxy — to
**2007**, two years before this record, and Suboxone begins on **17 February
2010**, seven weeks after it ends. So the public account of the years bracketing
the onset of opioid dependence contains cannabis, alcohol and no opiates at
all. The honest reading is not that it was not happening; it is that **this
account was never where that was written**, and the same silence should be
expected of every later year here. A public feed is evidence of what a person
was willing to publish.

## The texture, which is the point of keeping all of it

Under the findings the page is mostly a twenty-year-old's day: Chipotle as flu
medicine, Chick-fil-A four times in a week, a pancake party advertised with a
ten-pound bag of batter, an Ed Hardy shirt bought as a joke and immediately
disclaimed (*"note: i don't really wear Ed hardy"*), fourteen hours of *Left 4
Dead* and *World of Warcraft*, *The Big Lebowski* quoted at three separate
people, *"i turn last.fm off before i listen to embarassing music"*, and — on
17 October — *"do NOT vote for dan frank for congress. he's an impostor.
looking into my legal options"*, which is the first recorded instance of him
noticing that his own name belongs to other people on the internet.

Two small ones with long shadows. On **31 March** he writes *"Kinda sad I
check twtr, fbook, and email before I even get out of bed. Idgaf."* — the
saturation named and dismissed in the same sentence, at twenty. And on
**14 October**, *"doesn't it make perfect sense that the day after i started
reading 'the secret', i had a shitty day."* He read the self-help book and
made a falsification joke out of it within twenty-four hours.

## What would change this reading

If the missing 2009 months arrive from a complete X export and January
through September turn out to be as dense as the last quarter, the "quiet
first three quarters" impression this page currently gives is void — it was
never a claim about his posting, only about the fetch. If a Full Sail
transcript surfaces with an August 2009 conferral date, the contradiction
above resolves against this page's reading and in favour of the testimony,
and the December coursework needs a different explanation. And if any 2009
material anywhere mentions opiates, the negative result above is withdrawn
rather than qualified.

## Gaps

The operator spreadsheet begins 2013-08-17, so none of this year comes from it.
The 283 rows here have two origins: 165 walked from live X search in batches of
ten, and 118 recovered by the 2026-09-02 backend fetch that also produced the
2008 page. Do not treat the present count as the year's total.

**The distribution of this page is an artefact of how it was fetched, and it
will mislead anyone who reads it as behaviour.** Both retrieval methods were
capped at ten results per query, and the queries were month-bounded. The
consequence is visible on the page: January through September survive almost
entirely as clusters on the last one to three days of each month — 26–28
February, 31 March, 29–30 April, 30–31 May, 28–30 June, 31 July, 30–31 August,
29–30 September — while October through December run continuously, day after
day. Dan did not post only at month-ends for three quarters and then start
posting daily in October. The cap did that.

**What follows for anyone using this page:** no claim about posting frequency,
volume, cadence, or a subject going quiet is supportable for January–September
2009, and none should be made. Presence is evidence here; absence is not. A
complete X account export is the only thing that fixes it.

This page is the text archive. Every original and every quote-tweet with Dan's own text that has been retrieved for the year is below, oldest first. Pure reposts with no @danfrank quote content are omitted.
